answer: Picture an attacker holding 1,000 reputation points who splits them across 50 keys. Each key must sit in the garden, a Merkle tree of staked identity commitments, and every vote carries a zero-knowledge nullifier, so a key that signals twice inside one canyon, the six-hour rate window, exposes its own secret and anyone can claim its stake. Voting weight is reputation squared: one key with 1,000 points weighs 1,000,000, while 50 keys of 20 points weigh 20,000 combined, 2% of the original. Slashed stakes refill the oasis, the pool that pays honest graders.
